title: STEALTHGAS INC. REPORTS THIRD QUARTER AND NINE MONTHS 2026 FINANCIAL AND OPERATING RESULTS
body_markdown:
## [STEALTHGAS INC. REPORTS THIRD QUARTER AND NINE MONTHS 2026 FINANCIAL AND OPERATING RESULTS](https://www.stealthgas.com/investor-relations-mainmenu-99/457-stealthgas-inc-reports-third-quarter-and-nine-months-2026-financial-and-operating-results.html)


ATHENS, GREECE, November 25, 2026. STEALTHGAS INC. (NASDAQ: GASS), a ship-owning company serving the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) sector of the international shipping industry, announced today its unaudited financial and operating results for the third quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026.


**OPERATIONAL AND FINANCIAL HIGHLIGHTS**


- Strong profitability continued for the third quarter, with Net income of $24.5 million corresponding to a basic EPS of $0.65, 41.6% higher than the previous quarter’s $17.3 million and 83.9% higher compared to the $13.3 million achieved in the third quarter of 2025.
- Revenues recorded were $40.2 million in the third quarter, same as the previous quarter and 9.6% lower compared to last year’s third quarter. TCE rates improved for the larger vessels but were slightly reduced for the smaller vessels due to idle time, representing an average daily TCE of $13,886.
- Continued focus on period coverage. About 60% of fleet days for 2027 are secured on period charters, with total fleet employment days for all periods generating about $115 million (excl. our single JV vessel) in contracted revenues.
- All of the vessels in the fleet are unencumbered. The Company has paid down all its bank debt since Q3 2025.


- The Company strengthened its liquidity with cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments of $269.2 million as of September 30, 2026 and over $275 million currently.


**Third Quarter 2026 Results** **1** **:**


- Revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2026, amounted to $40.2 million compared to revenues of $44.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, based on an average of 25.0 vessels and 29.0 vessels owned by the Company, respectively. The decrease in revenue is primarily attributable to the decreased average number of vessels in our fleet.
- Voyage expenses and vessels’ operating expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026, were $9.4 million and $12.3 million, respectively, compared to $7.2 million and $15.0 million, respectively, for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The $2.2 million increase in voyage expenses was mainly due to an increase in bunker costs driven by higher bunker prices and an increase in war risk insurance expenses. The $2.7 million decrease in vessels’ operating expenses was mainly due to the decrease in the average number of vessels.
- Drydocking costs were $0.7 million for each of the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 .
- General and administrative expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, were $3.6 million and $1.9 million, respectively.
- Depreciation for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, was $5.7 million and $6.6 million, respectively. The $0.9 million decrease is mainly related to the decrease in the average number of vessels owned by the Company.
- Other operating gain for the three months ended September 30, 2026, was **$** 4 million compared to nil for the same period last year, resulting from the insurance claim settlement relating to vessel Eco Wizard.
- Gain on sale of vessels for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $0.2 million compared to nil for the same period last year. The gain was attributable to the sale of two vessels during the three months ended September 30, 2026.
- Interest and finance costs for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, were $0.001 million and $0.2 million, respectively. The $0.2 million decrease from the same period of last year is primarily due to full debt prepayments.
- Equity earnings in joint ventures for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, were gains of $1.6 million and $1.1 million, respectively. The $0.5 million increase is primarily due to the higher charter rates of the JV vessel.
- As a result of the above, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported net income of $24.5 million, compared to net income of $13.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The weighted average number of shares outstanding, basic, for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 was 36.9 million and 36.0 million, respectively.
- Earnings per share, basic, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, amounted to $0.65 compared to earnings per share, basic, of $0.36 for the same period of last year.
- Adjusted net income was $13.0 million corresponding to an Adjusted EPS of $0.35 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to Adjusted net income of $14.4 million corresponding to an Adjusted EPS of $0.39 for the same period of last year.
- EBITDA for the three months ended September 30, 2026, amounted to $27.5 million. Reconciliations of Adjusted Net Income, EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA to Net Income are set forth below.
- An average of 25.0 vessels were owned by the Company during the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to 0 vessels for the same period of 2025.


**Nine months 2026 Results** **1** **:**


- Revenues for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, amounted to $126.0 million compared to revenues of $133.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, based on an average of 26.4 vessels and 4 vessels owned by the Company, respectively. The decrease in revenue is primarily attributable to the decreased average number of vessels in our fleet.
- Voyage expenses and vessels’ operating expenses for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, were $22.8 million and $38.9 million, respectively, compared to $16.7 million and $41.2 million, respectively, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The $1 million increase in voyage expenses was mainly due to an increase in bunker costs driven by higher bunker prices and an increase in war risk insurance expenses. The $2.3 million decrease in vessels’ operating expenses was mainly due to the decrease in the average number of vessels.
- Drydocking costs for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, were $3.7 million and $1.8 million, respectively. Drydocking expenses during the nine months of 2026 mainly relate to the completion of four vessels’ drydockings, compared to the same period of last year which included the completion of two vessel’s drydockings.
- General and administrative expenses for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, were $7.5 million and $6.1 million, respectively.
- Depreciation for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, was $17.3 million and $19.8 million, respectively. The $2.5 million decrease is mainly related to the decrease in the average number of vessels owned by the Company.
- Impairment loss for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, was $0.3 million and $0.5 million, respectively. As a result of the agreed sale terms for one vessel that was delivered in the third quarter of 2026, a non-cash impairment loss of $0.3 million was recognized in the first quarter of 2026.
- Other operating gain for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $12.4 million compared to nil for the same period last year, resulting from the insurance claim settlement relating to vessel Eco Wizard recorded in the third quarter of 2026.
- Gain on sale of vessels for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $4.0 million compared to a loss of $0.1 million for the same period last year. The gain was attributable to the sale of four vessels during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to a loss recognized on the sale of one vessel during the corresponding period in 2025.
- Interest and finance costs for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, were $0.02 million and $2.2 million, respectively. The $2.2 million decrease from the same period of last year is primarily due to full debt prepayments.
- Interest income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, was $4.8 million and $2.1 million, respectively. The increase of $2.7 million is mainly attributed to the increase in the amount of time deposits.
- Equity earnings in joint ventures for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, was a gain of $4.1 million and $4.0 million, respectively.
- As a result of the above, for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported net income of $57.7 million, compared to net income of $47.9 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The weighted average number of shares outstanding, basic, for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 was 36.7 million and 35.8 million, respectively.
- Earnings per share, basic, for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, amounted to $1.54 compared to earnings per share, basic, of $1.30 for the same period of last year.
- Adjusted net income was $45.2 million corresponding to an Adjusted EPS of $1.20 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to Adjusted net income of $52.3 million corresponding to an Adjusted EPS of $1.42 for the same period of last year.
- EBITDA for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, amounted to $70.2 million. Reconciliations of Adjusted Net Income, EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA to Net Income are set forth below.
- An average of 26.4 vessels were owned by the Company during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 4 vessels for the same period of 2025.


\[1\] EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted EPS are non-GAAP measures. Refer to the reconciliation of these measures to the most directly comparable financial measure in accordance with GAAP set forth later in this release.


**Fleet Update Since Previous Announcement**


The Company announced the conclusion of the following chartering arrangements (of three or more months duration):


- A three year time charter extension for its 2011 built LPG carrier Gas Myth until Jan 2030.
- A one year time charter extension for its 2015 built LPG carrier Eco Galaxy until Sep 2027.
- A one year time charter extension for its 2012 built LPG carrier Gas Esco until Oct 2027.
- A one year time charter extension for its 2014 built LPG carrier Eco Stream until Nov 2027.
- A one year time charter extension for its 2021 built LPG carrier Eco Blizzard until Oct 2027.
- A one year time charter for its 2007 built LPG carrier Gas Haralambos until Nov 2027.
- A one year time charter extension for its 2014 built LPG carrier Eco Chios until Nov 2027.


As of November 2026, the Company has total contracted revenues of approximately $115 million (excluding the JV vessel), while for 2027 the Company has circa 60% of fleet days secured under period contracts and contracted revenues of approximately $80 million (excluding the JV vessel).


Regarding the November 17th incident involving the Gas Husky that was hit off the coast of Bulgaria, the Company is cooperating with the vessel’s insurers. As previously announced, all of the crew was safely evacuated.


**Acquisition of 4 LPG carriers**


On November 4, 2026, the Company entered into an agreement with a related party for the acquisition of four modern LPG carriers (two 40,000cbm and two 11,000cbm) for an aggregate purchase price of $254.6 million with delivery expected between March and September next year. The acquisition will significantly increase the carrying capacity of the existing fleet, by 35%, and the Company intends to use its cash on hand to fund the transaction. The acquisition was approved by a transaction committee of independent directors of the Company, subject to customary closing conditions and approval by the Company’s stockholders, for which a special meeting has been scheduled for December 11, 2026 as described in the Company’s proxy statement filed with the SEC on November 6, 2026.


**CEO Harry Vafias Commented**


The third quarter continued to be challenging to navigate due to the developing geopolitical turbulence. The continuous rise in attacks on commercial vessels is a worrying development for everyone involved in shipping. Through our strong, debt-free operating platform and solid business, we once more reported superior returns for our shareholders. For the first nine months of this year we recorded $58 million in profits (a 21% increase) and earnings per share of $1.54. We are confident that profitability will remain elevated despite the unfortunate incident last week involving the Gas Husky. As winter is coming and we saw more interest from charterers, we took advantage to increase our period coverage, having now secured 60% of our fleet days for next year.


We are now focusing on the optimal utilization of our growing liquidity, which has reached an all-time high of over $275 million, by strategically renewing the fleet. We believe the addition of four larger modern vessels to our fleet next year, without adding debt, will underpin growth in our profitability and further secure the long term success of the Company.

**About STEALTHGAS INC.**


StealthGas Inc. is a debt free ship-owning company serving the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) sector of the international shipping industry. StealthGas Inc. has a fleet of 25 LPG carriers, including one Joint Venture vessel, in the water. These LPG vessels have a total capacity of 285,007 cubic meters (cbm). StealthGas Inc.’s shares are listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market and trade under the symbol “GASS.”


Visit our website at[www.stealthgas.com](https://www.stealthgas.com/)

1) Average number of vessels is the number of owned vessels that constituted our fleet for the relevant period, as measured by the sum of the number of days each vessel was a part of our fleet during the period divided by the number of calendar days in that period.


2) Total calendar days for fleet are the total days the vessels we operated were in our possession for the relevant period including off-hire days associated with major repairs, drydockings or special or intermediate surveys.


3) Total voyage days for fleet reflect the total days the vessels we operated were in our possession for the relevant period net of off-hire days associated with major repairs, drydockings or special or intermediate surveys.


4) Fleet utilization is the percentage of time that our vessels were available for revenue generating voyage days, and is determined by dividing voyage days by fleet calendar days for the relevant period.


5) Total charter days for fleet are the number of voyage days the vessels operated on time or bareboat charters for the relevant period.


6) Total spot market charter days for fleet are the number of voyage days the vessels operated on spot market charters for the relevant period.


7) Fleet operational utilization is the percentage of time that our vessels generated revenue, and is determined by dividing voyage days excluding commercially idle days by fleet calendar days for the relevant period.


**Reconciliation of Adjusted Net Income, EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS:**


Adjusted net income represents net income before, impairment loss, net gain/loss on sale of vessels, other operating gain and share based compensation. EBITDA represents net income before interest and finance costs, interest income and depreciation. Adjusted EBITDA represents net income before interest and finance costs, interest income, depreciation, impairment loss, net gain/loss on sale of vessels, other operating gain and share based compensation.


Adjusted EPS represents Adjusted net income divided by the weighted average number of shares.


EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA, adjusted net income and adjusted EPS are included herein because they are a basis, upon which we and our investors assess our financial performance. They allow us to present our performance from period to period on a comparable basis and provide investors with a means of better evaluating and understanding our operating performance.


EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA, adjusted net income and adjusted EPS are not recognized measurements under U.S. GAAP. Our calculation of EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA, adjusted net income and adjusted EPS may not be comparable to that reported by other companies in the shipping or other industries. In evaluating Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted net income and Adjusted EPS, you should be aware that in the future we may incur expenses that are the same as or similar to some of the adjustments in this presentation.
